messages:
Julia: FYI incoming enterprise ask from FinServe — they want a single commitment that covers multi-region traffic (us-east + eu-west), predictable p99 latency for chat (~<250ms), and a POA for reserved GPUs + autoscale. Can SRE/solutions weigh in on pooled vs per-region reserve and a quick cost sketch?
Mike: quick note — reserved GPUs are region-scoped. You can approximate a "pooled" experience with route-aware failover + reserved capacity in each region and a global routing policy, but true cross-region pooling requires warm standby and routing latency tradeoffs.
Anika: For sizing we need their RPS, avg tokens per request, and token distribution tail. If they share 24h sample traffic we can produce a realistic batch/cache strategy. Without that, a rough heuristic: reserved = steady-state 80th percentile RPS * per-request GPU cost factor; burst via autoscale.
Julia: They gave rough numbers: 5k peak rps, avg 80 tokens/request, chat model ~8 tokens/sec per GPU (quantized). They asked about a 40 GPU commit as a starting point.
Mike: That 40-GPU commit could hit target if we do: regional split 60/40 (us-east/eu-west), aggressive prefix/KV cache, and model quantization. Recommend 20% headroom for autoscale buffer and prewarm slots. Also plan a preheat window before business hours.
Anika: Also recommend model variants: quantized v1 (faster, lower cost) and fp16 v2 (fallback). Route by cost/latency. This reduces required reserved GPUs by ~25% at cost of slight quality diff.
Raj: Operational constraints: reserved pools are per-AZ/region. Autoscale policies can borrow from reserved if configured as "burst from reserved". If you want cross-region fallback, we must configure global routing + warm KV replication — adds 5–10% perf hit on failover.
Tina: Security / compliance asks: FinServe requires KMS-backed key management, customer-managed key (CMK), and verbose audit logs for model inputs/outputs for 30 days. Are those supported in Private/Dedicated?
Anika: Yes for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can support CMK in VPC or private plane options but we need to confirm retention window. I'll add that to the checklist.
Evan: Pricing note: two quick options — (A) 40 reserved GPUs across regions (split 24/16) -> estimated list ~$XXXk/mo (ballpark) + overage at per-token; (B) Hybrid: reserve 28 GPUs + 20k burst credits -> lowers commit by ~25% but higher unit overage. I'll send a formal quote.
Julia: Could you sketch the autoscale config we’d hand to their infra team? want to show prewarm + burst rules.
Mike: Example autoscale snippet (informal):
```json
{
  "policy": "priority",
  "reserved_pool": {"region": "us-east", "gpus": 24},
  "reserved_pool_eu": {"region": "eu-west", "gpus": 16},
  "burst": {"max_gpus": 60, "burst_credits": 20000},
  "prewarm": {"enabled": true, "window": "20m", "slots": 8},
  "fallback": {"route_on_capacity": true, "fallback_model": "quant-v1"}
}
```
Mike: Key ops rules: 1) keep prewarm slot count small and scheduled, 2) autoscale cool-down 30s for chat, 3) prefer prefix cache hits before spinning new containers.
Anika: For the POC: we should run a short 48h profiling run with traces (token lengths, p50/p95/p99 latencies) — that will let us recommend concrete reserved numbers and a cache warm-up plan.
Julia: I'll ask FinServe for the 24h trace and send the security questionnaire to Tina.
Tina: Thanks — once I have the questionnaire back I'll confirm CMK + audit retention and flag any gaps.
capacity-bot: Quote generated (draft): commit-40gpus-hybrid-estimate_v1 — est $128,400/mo (internal).
Evan: I'll formalize two options in a PDF and include the POC runbook and expected unit economics for quant vs fp16.
Julia: Awesome. Next steps: 1) FinServe provide 24h traffic sample + completed security form, 2) we run 48h profiling, 3) produce final reserved/auto plan and quote. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Raj: noted, will prep runbook for KV replication and cross-region warm standby.
Anika: will draft the POC checklist and a short script to collect token distribution.
Tina: will review security answers and reply with any blocking items within 48h.
Julia: I'll follow up with FinServe and update thread.
